The point $P$ is located on the unit circle, as shown above. The $y$-coordinate of $P$ is $\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}.$ What is the $x$-coordinate of $P?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the point $P$ lies on the unit circle, it must satisfy the Pythagorean theorem: 

$$
{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1
$$

Substituting $y=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}$ into the above and solving for $x$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & =1 \\ {x}^{2}+{(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3})}^{2} & =1 \\ {x}^{2}+(\frac{5}{9}) & =1 \\ {x}^{2} & =1-\frac{5}{9} \\ {x}^{2} & =\frac{4}{9} \\ x & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{4}{9}} \\ x & =\pm \frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we select the negative answer since $x$ is negative in the second quadrant. So our final answer is $x=-\frac{2}{3}.$
